findings.location: sections/40-word-in-the-heart.tex lines 15-17 (web Markdown line 463, the last sentence of the opening paragraph of 'While Men Slept: The Field Kept by the Word That Dwells in the Heart')
findings.problem: "They are set together here because both ask something of each hearer" names the study's own joining of the parable and Col 3:16 instead of stating the connection. This is the editor's synthesis labelled in the body, which 'State the finding, not the process that produced it' in guidance/editorial.md excludes; deleting the clause loses nothing. It is the only instance found in the study, so it does not block.
findings.required_result: State the connection without the process clause, keeping the preceding qualification that Chrysostom does not set the two passages side by side. For example: "Both ask something of each hearer: the parable, as Chrysostom reads it, asks him to stay awake, and Paul says what he is to keep in his heart."

observations.location: sections/20-patience-of-the-field.tex lines 38, 97, 176 and 186; sections/30-cry-from-captivity.tex line 192; sections/40-word-in-the-heart.tex lines 42, 45 and 106
observations.note: These eight inner quotations close with the TeX sequence ''' (for example `Wilt Thou?'''). A pdflatex test under the leaf's T1/lmodern setup sets that as a double closing quote followed by a single one (‘Wilt Thou?”’), so the native print edition nests the marks the wrong way round, while the web reader sets ‘Wilt Thou?’” correctly; writing '\,'' gives the right order in both. No screen or review criterion covers this sequence, which points to a missing typography lint rather than to anything particular to this leaf.

observations.location: sections/20-patience-of-the-field.tex lines 153 and 156 (Augustine, Ep. 93.34 and 93.36, quoted from NPNF)
observations.note: The quotations "at the end of the world,--meanwhile" and "even to apostles,--namely" copy the CCEL plain text, which writes its dashes as ASCII -- (the same file has "formless;--on account"). In TeX, -- sets an en dash, so the print and web editions both show "world,–meanwhile"; the printed NPNF very likely has an em dash there (---), but this was not checked against page images.
